simplified: How far AO falls for a given wetness is an estimate. On a real board it depends on how much water there is, where it lies and how clean it is.
The sensing board is drawn as part of the module; on the real one it is a separate board on two wires.
The tracks do not corrode. Real ones do when left powered while wet.
Its comparator switches cleanly at the trimmer's setting. A real one flickers when the reading sits right at that point.
The resistances inside the module are estimates; no schematic of the kit's module has been seen.
The comparator and the two indicator lights draw a few milliamps that are not counted.
